Orthopedics · published research

Fractures (wrist/hand)

Small wrist-fracture trials report some improvements in pain, strength, or motion, but one trial found no improvement in patient-rated pain or function during casting.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Small wrist-fracture trials report some improvements in pain, strength, or motion, but one trial found no improvement in patient-rated pain or function during casting.

Summary of the Evidence

The broad Bone > Fractures category contains 17 unique titles: seven human studies, four animal studies, three meta-analyses, one review, one protocol, and one cost-effectiveness analysis. Only three human randomized trials directly concern wrist or hand fractures. The remaining fracture records address other anatomical sites, so their findings are not direct evidence for wrist or hand recovery.

Human and clinical evidence

In a 50-person trial after wrist or hand fracture, 830-nm near-infrared laser treatment was associated with improvements in selected clinical measures (Chang et al. 2014). A 53-person trial delivered PBM while participants were in a cast. Patient-rated pain and function did not differ, although night pain and some strength or motion measures improved (Sæbø et al. 2021). A later 50-person study after cast removal and during exercise reported better patient-rated function and lower pain or analgesic use at several follow-up points (Sæbø et al. 2022). These are three separate trial publications, but do not justify a general conclusion for all fractures.

Animal evidence

Four animal studies in the broad category include two rat and two rabbit studies. Their fracture-healing results are preclinical and should not be combined with patient-reported recovery.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro or ex-vivo study was identified in the exact fracture category.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The wrist and hand trials used 830-nm near-infrared light or 904-nm near-infrared laser. One protocol used 60 mW and 9.7 J/cm² over ten sessions in two weeks; the cast study used nine sessions over three weeks, and the post-cast study treated alongside exercises. The source records concern distinct phases of recovery, which limits direct comparison. One country field is ambiguous and is retained as such rather than assigned to either listed country.

Interpretation

Some short-term outcomes improve in small trials, but results vary by timing and measure. The broad fracture reviews and animal models do not settle the effect for distal-radius or hand fractures.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for patient-rated wrist function after PBM during recovery from a distal-radius fracture Very low for consistent pain or healing benefit across fracture types
Publications and records17 unique titles in broad Bone > Fractures category

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The broad fracture category contains only three directly relevant wrist or hand trials, while other records concern different bones and animal models. The direct randomized trials differ by treatment timing and report mixed subjective and objective outcomes. Larger independent trials with common fracture criteria, measures, and follow-up would clarify applicability.
